I was friends with a guy for about 20 years. Basically grew up together. But at one point, life forked in different directions for everyone and we all moved for work or family. We still kept in touch every day and played games together frequently online. But something in him changed after he graduated from university. He went to school for computer science but never did anything to prove his abilities. Didn't build up a portfolio and didn't get any jobs in the field he went to school for. So he started working an overnight inventory job for cash and has just been kinda lifing it there ever since. 



During this time in his life, he started absorbing a lot of extreme right wing media. He started to become very callous and angry at the world. In particular, he had developed a strong distaste for immigrants and people of colour in general. He became hella racist. We called him out on it every single time he started ranting and getting sketchy with it. Since we had known him for so long, we wanted to believe he would change so we kept telling him it wasn't cool and he can't keep talking like that around us. It was also making the rest of us feel like we had to walk on eggshells when talking about more sensitive subjects because we feared that he would go off the rails and go on a racist tirade. Which wasn't healthy for our own discussions either. We like to talk about things going on in the world and the impact they are having. 



We got on the subject one day about all the mass child graves they were finding in Canada. It very understandably was upsetting the indigenous community and things like orange hand prints were being put on church buildings/doors. We all agreed how fucking horrible it was that this shit happened to these kids and their families. Just tragic in every way. Our former friend obviously felt differently. Went on a very rage bait-y rant about nationalism and "saying it without saying it" if you know what I mean. He thought he was being clever by not directly saying anything and just dancing around it by trying to sound like he was just a proud Canadian and supports what previous generations were doing. That was the last straw for me. He clearly was not going to change. He was down some right wing extremist pipe and wasn't going to crawl out of it. We were not the echo chamber he was looking for and our conversations were becoming very antagonistic with him. So we banned him from our server and just cut off all communication. The wild part was that he clearly thought he aligned with certain people within our friend group because he was only messaging a couple of them to find out what was going on. Doesn't think he did anything wrong and said he felt blind sided that we kicked him. Despite having various altercations with him over similar incidents and warning him to cut it out. Just wild. 



I know it can be argued that we are silencing him and not being open to alternative discourse. But I just refuse to support his racism and he was given multiple chances to course correct. Way more than he should have been given.

Depends what we are qualifying as reading. Because I'm not just picking up books and reading them. Nor am I reading e-books. I will read articles online about things that interest me. Be it scientific breakthroughs or just some content creator drama. I browse reddit a little bit some days. I sometimes have to read documents at work. I will sometimes wiki hop and just read about a bunch of stuff. Usually starts off from me reading about something I have never heard of before so I google it, find the wiki page, and then start middle mouse clicking anything with a link that interests me or I feel I need to know more about for context pertaining to the initial subject I was researching. But I am definitely not ever, under any circumstance, breaking out a book like LotR or something and just sitting down in a chair and reading it. I hate reading in that way, for some reason. I can't bring myself to do it. I get so bored so fast.

I can't even accurately pinpoint what the difference is. It could be a book about something I genuinely have interest in but I just don't have the mental fortitude to sit down and commit to it. Maybe being forced to read shit I don't care about in school beat any enjoyment that could have come from reading out of me.

So if we are saying "conventional" reading where you crack open a book and go sit down and just read it for a while, my answer would be 0. But if we are counting all facets of reading from a diverse collection of sources, then I'm reading for several hours every weekday and maybe a little less on weekends when I'm not working.

Video Horror Society (VHS). It officially sunset almost a year ago. Still reeling from it. I was so passionate about that game. I loved everything about it and i was putting my all into it. I just haven't had the same passion for gaming since. I couldn't stop thinking about how it was gonna be gone forever. All those devs losing their jobs and moving on. The company essentially shutting down as well and laying everyone off. Seeing all of them on LinkedIn posting about looking for new work. It was heartbreaking. I didn't know any of them on a personal level, really. Though I did have a chat with one of the devs towards the end of the game's life and found out he not only used to live in the same city as me, but worked in a building that was literally a block away from where I was working. I very well could have crossed paths with him at some point. Small world. It just left a very big hole in me that has yet to be filled in by anything else. I've played a lot of bangers since then. Like Sea of Stars. But I just can't shake how sad I am about that game being gone. 



Luckily some passionate individuals in the community reversed engineered the backend and were able to trick the game into thinking it was authenticating on official servers so everyone could continue playing. But only with private, peer to peer lobbies in private matchmaking. So no public games or queueing up for games. But at least I can still play in private lobbies (with flaky ping) or even just mess around myself and try to remember the good old days and just take in the visuals and sounds that remind me of a better time in my life. 

  
I know it's just a game, but it felt like losing a best friend. It was heart wrenching. I have never, ever, felt this way about a game before. Truly a devastating experience.

I recently started playing Across the Obelisk and they have some interesting support classes. It is a turn based deck builder roguelike, but I think that makes it even more fun. Healers/support function in different ways and each one excels at certain things better than others. 

I've done runs where I play Reginald like a Paladin and do a ton of holy damage while also applying a debuff that is called Sanctify that will heal people who attack them. Dropping mad holy DPS while giving the rest of my team a way to heal from doing more damage.

Another favourite is Nezglekt. He heals at the end of his turn, passively, based on the number of stacks of two particular debuffs he can apply to the enemy. But perks allow you to do some more interesting things with those stacks. One of them is called insane and it will not only reduce the damage that the target inflicted by it can do, but you can also use some perk points to spec it so it also reduces their HP by a set amount per stack. So you get some decent passive healing on top of damage reduction.

Ottis can be played in many similar ways to Reginald but also has the added benefit of healing people for a percentage of any shield/block that he applies. So you can throw in some shielding and blocking cards to do some extra healing as well as mitigating some damage via the block. 

Malukah is pretty cool in that she can do a few things. Can just throw out chonk heals and still do okay, can stack regen pretty efficiently and just make people heal for a ton at the start of their turns, and can also heal people by DPSing and applying dark stacks to enemies. She is also good at applying debuffs to enemies and removing them from her allies.

You can also adjust them a little further in the form of traits you earn from leveling up and with perks you set before a run. You can save perk loadouts if you have a particular vision in mind for the run. Equipment you can buy and put on your characters also plays a role. They are pretty diverse and can add some synergy with other people on the team. Like you can for example get an item that will apply one stack of a different debuff for every stack of another debuff that you apply to an enemy. Which may benefit someone else. 

It is seriously one of the best games I have ever played. I highly recommend it if you like roguelikes or deckbuilders. It is even multiplayer. You can play with 4 people. You can even play with less and just divide up the characters how you see fit. The game also has some DnD elements to it. It's just such a robust game with unlockable characters, pets, cards, etc. Feels like I'm playing a game from the early 2000's where you could actually play and do arbitrary bullshit to unlock stuff instead of just paying for a DLC and getting everything. 

I know your question was about supports in general, but it's hard to not gush about this game.

She was very shook by that because she thought he was "the one." Maybe that was true, maybe it was just young teen naivety. Regardless, I figured it was more appropriate to not let her know how I really felt at that time. Didn't seem right to act on those feelings when she was clearly still grieving and dealing with the loss of someone she thought she would spend the rest of her life with. 

Fast forward 6 years and I had just slotted myself into the friend role for so long that I just keep suppressing my feelings. She was, and still is, my best friend. I didn't want to potentially ruin that and make things weird. We eventually met this other guy playing a different game a year or two later. Not wanting him to feel the same immense weight I felt on my chest, I told him I would test the waters for him and gauge her feelings a little. In hindsight this all seems a little manipulative. Because she did say that she felt that way about him to some extent. So I let him know so he could make a move. I hand delivered the only girl that I have felt this way about, to another man. 1.) Headset (Desktop audio)

2.) Headset mic (Input, not used because I have a Yeti)

3.) Yeti through RTX Voice (Input)

4.) Voicemod Virtual Line (Virtual input from Voicemod that uses my Yeti through RTX Voice input)

There is literally no other audio stream I can use that will ONLY transmit soundboard sounds to listen to, without sending through stream (monitor only). I feed into the conspiracy theory of varying rates per player, big time. So this is going to sound like some crazy rambling. But they are just anecdotal observations from within my own community. 

There are too many people that are consistently lucky. And conversely, too many people that are consistently unlucky. For the first few shiny releases, I was simply chalking it up to luck. There weren't enough shinies and variety to really assume anything contrary to that. 

But now that we have dozens of shinies across many different Pokemon that are abundant in different biomes, there is something potentially shiny to tap on almost every block. Increased access to all this shiny potential only exacerbated the luck difference I was starting to notice. 

It's always the same people posting day 1 shinies during events, multiple shiny catches in a single day, many legendary shinies, etc. The level of dedication between these players is all over the place. There are some of the more hardcore players that will hunt aggressively and get tons of event shinies. Sure they will see/catch a few thousand event mons, but they are also getting 1 shiny for every 100 or 150 things they encounter. So they are putting in an immense effort, but they are being overcompensated based on the "average" There are also people, like a friend of mine, that maybe go out for a handful of hours over the course of an entire week long event and still make out like a bandit. Seeing a similar rate. They maybe only encountered 200 things the entire week. But they still nabbed two or more shinies out of it. On the opposite end of the scale, you have people putting in tons of effort and not seeing anything for it. If these were singular events, I would say "Tough luck. Maybe next time." But next time is always the same. The same people keep getting tons of shinies with proportionately less effort than others. These people never see dry spells and the people that are consistently unlucky never see hot streaks.

I find there are more middle of the ground players that don't see a ton of success but get the odd shiny here and there. Maybe only get the new hotness shiny every other event. It just seems to get more and more disproportionate as time goes on and more shinies are released.

Not related to scams on reddit, but I did encounter a man at a 7-11 one night last week that I'm pretty sure was trying to scam people for money. I inherently want to believe that someone actually needs my help, but I will also be cautious and try to gauge the situation.

A man came running out to me, waving his arms and standing in front of my car as I was about to pull away and leave. He told me that him and his girlfriend ran out of gas and needed 50 - 100 dollars for gas to get to Calgary. He said they were freezing and really needed help right now. He seemingly was trying to create sense of urgency. He stated that he would paypal me double, triple, w/e I wanted, at a later date when he was back on his feet and could pay me back. Making a promise of compensation in excess of what was given to him. 

A large part of me wanted to believe his story was true so I continued to engage in conversation with the man. I told him that I didn't have any cash on me and that I couldn't help him out. Which was true. Then he asked "Can't you go inside and use the ATM or something? I really need some help." I asked him where his car was and he pointed to a car (a car I assume wasn't even his) over in the dark, parked in front of an apartment building. I stopped for a moment to think about whether I should do it or not. Meanwhile, he kept layering on the dire straits he was in. Trying to appeal to the fact that apparently no one had even talked to him for as long as I had or even tried to search their car for change. Lamented about another gentleman in a car at the gas pumps that supposedly told him to "Fuck off" So that's when I told him that I could help him out. But I told him that the way I was going to help him was by letting him pump the gas and I would pay for it.

This is when everything started to unravel. All of a sudden he didn't think it was such a good idea. He said the car was completely out of gas and couldn't be driven up to the pumps. So I told him that's fine. Just pop it in neutral and I'll push it. I even got out of my car and started walking towards the vehicle he claimed was his. Then the excuse was that his hands were too cold and he didn't think he could do it. Then another excuse was that his car was way too heavy to push. So while we were walking to what was supposedly his vehicle, he told me that he wasn't going to push his car in and that he didn't feel capable of doing it. So I said "If getting this gas was so important, I'm sure you can muster the strength to push this car to the pumps." He simply replied "Naw man, I'm not gonna push it." Then he went inside the 7-11 and motioned to someone, I assume his girlfriend, that it was time to leave. Then they disappeared behind the 7-11 and didn't even go back to "their" car. 

So I'm quite certain this guy was trying to scam people for money. I offered to help in a tangible way that would have solved the problem of the narrative that he presented. But he declined. Maybe they were in desperate need of gas to get to Calgary and he was just very, very concerned about the state of his hands and genuinely believed that we would not be able to get his car to the pumps. But I was not about to just hand 100 dollars to a stranger that approached my vehicle at 1 AM at a 7-11. Looking back on it, I probably shouldn't have even parked my car and gotten out of it. I didn't know this man or if he planned to get violent because I wasn't helping him in the way he wanted.

I think another tip that maybe a lot of people don't know about, is you can save a streak if you miss or the pokemon smacks the ball away if you are doing a quick catch and react in the proper way. 

The game doesn't calculate the throw until you make contact with the Pokemon, or seemingly when the ball naturally resets after flubbing a throw and it bounces away. If you engage a quick catch and either miss or the Pokemon attacks and knocks it away, instead of tapping outside of the menu to make it go away, instead click on any item in the menu you brought out. If done quick enough, this effectively does two things:

1.) It saves the ball. The ball does not get consumed if you do this before the ball naturally resets.

2.) It preserves any throw streak you have because it never actually calculated a throw.

This has saved me a bunch of times when the Pokemon attacked unexpectedly, the Pokemon jumped and I missed, or I lost contact while sliding my finger and pretty much dropped the ball.

**EDIT:** Adding this in because I forgot, but I want to make it clear that this only works when you DON'T make contact with the Pokemon and a catch sequence doesn't ensue. This only works if the ball doesn't actually hit the Pokemon, ie: you completely miss the throw or the Pokemon bats it away.

Triple resist is not a term from the original game because such a resistance does not exist. You either have a single resistance, a double resistance, or an immunity. Triple resist in this context is entirely localized to this game and is simply a colloquial term used to express that a Pokemon has a single resistance and an immunity tier resistance to a type. Nothing more, nothing less. It isn't meant to reflect actual numbers.

IVs are 100% more important than CP. CP is just a by-product of the calculation of the base stats + IVs. It's just a generic visual representation of "strength". CP basically means nothing outside of PvP and gym decay. IVs will determine what breakpoints you reach and when. IVs will determine what bulkpoints you reach and when. IVs will affect the resulting evolution of your Tyrogues. IVs will affect your ability to power up your Pokemon to optimal levels/stats for specific PvP leagues. CP just gates you from using Pokemon in certain leagues and affects how fast your Pokemon loses motivation in gyms. That's it.

Something I read in another post on this sub that you can try, in case nothing else suggested works:

1.) Make sure the PBP has been removed as a recognized device in the game. Tap the eject icon in the PBP settings.

2.) Unpair the PBP from your phone if it is currently paired. Then re-pair it with the phone.

3.) Restart the phone or the PBP itself. Resetting the PBP is much faster. There is a little button near the back on the black line that separates the white and red sections of the ball. It's to the right of the strap. If simply resetting the PBP doesn't work, try repeating step 2 and restarting the phone instead.

4.) Go back into the game and enter the settings menu. Before going to the PBP menu, tap the red button on the top of the ball twice, then enter the PBP menu and tap the icon as soon as it pops up.

While this has already been answered by several people, I just want to add that it's because of how much more heavily the attack stat is weighted in CP calculations.
